articles.title: 2003 Messier Marathon and SJAA Activities
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) announced its 2003 Messier Marathon, a major observing event held on March 29/30 at Henry Coe State Park, challenging participants to locate 109 deep-sky objects in one night. The article details the event's history, practical advice for participants, and mentions associated guides like Don Machholz's booklet. Furthermore, it provides a comprehensive calendar of SJAA activities for March and April, including star parties, general meetings, and astronomy classes.

articles.title: Messier Side Dishes
articles.summary: This article, 'Messier Side Dishes,' encourages amateur astronomers, particularly during a Messier marathon, to explore additional celestial objects often overlooked near famous Messier catalogue entries. It provides a guide to finding intriguing non-Messier deep-sky objects, such as galaxies, nebulae, and clusters, that are within a degree of well-known Messiers like M31, M42, M65/M66, and M13. The aim is to enrich the observing experience by highlighting these 'side dishes' and turning the marathon into a more comprehensive celestial 'gourmet meal'.

articles.title: Board of Directors elected for 2003
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) held its corporate annual meeting in February 2003 to elect its Board of Directors. Dana Crom, along with Craig and Elena Scull, were newly elected, while Jim Van Nuland, Bill O'Shaughnessy, and Bob Havner were re-elected. The new board will proceed to elect its officers at the upcoming March meeting.

articles.title: Pre-register now for the April 13 SJAA auction
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is announcing its 23rd annual auction and swap on April 13, urging participants to pre-register items, especially large or numerous ones, by emailing descriptions and photos to auction@sjaa.net. This event serves as a fundraiser for the club's loaner program, with all commissions being tax-deductible due to SJAA's 501(c)(3) status.

articles.title: Mooning
articles.summary: This article explores the concept of creating a 3D stereogram of the Moon by photographing it at the same phase across different lunar cycles to capture distinct librations. Author Dave North discusses the technical challenges of timing these shots to achieve significant east/west libration shift while minimizing north/south changes, explaining how such an image would make the Moon appear as close as three feet away. The piece delves into practical timing calculations and software recommendations, posing an ongoing problem for amateur astrophotographers.

articles.title: Planets to in-Vesta-gate in March
articles.summary: The article highlights prime viewing opportunities for Jupiter and Saturn in March, detailing features like Jupiter's pink Great Red Spot and Saturn's visible ring gaps and spokes. It also encourages observers to target asteroid (4) Vesta, which reaches opposition on March 26th, noting its potential resolvability with large telescopes and unique geological characteristics. Mars is also briefly mentioned as a morning object, while directions to Houge Park suggest a local astronomy event context.

articles.title: Upcoming Programs and Events
articles.summary: The article details several upcoming astronomy-related events for March, including a series of school star parties across various locations in the San Jose area. It also announces a program by Robert Naeye on 'Solving the universe's mysteries through extra dimensions' and a Silicon Valley Astronomy Lecture Series event featuring Dr. Seth Shostak discussing the protocol for responding to a message from space.

articles.title: Celestial calendar March 2003
articles.summary: This celestial calendar for March 2003 provides detailed astronomical information including lunar phases, planetary positions, magnitudes, and rise/set/transit times for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. It also lists solar data such as hours of darkness and astronomical twilight, sidereal time, and identifies the darkest Saturday night for observing during the month.

articles.title: SJAA loaner scope status
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) operates a loaner telescope program, making various astronomical scopes available to its members. Members can contact Mike Koop to borrow equipment, with detailed lists provided for scopes currently available, those recently loaned out, and those on extended loan. The article also includes a waiting list for popular items, outlining the status and contact information for borrowing.
